patch.description:
Requires platform administrator access. Send either `action` or an edit containing `assigned_policy`, `labels`, or both. Both edits succeed together or neither changes.

Actions are `cordon`, `drain`, `revoke`, `rotate`, and `self_test`. Revocation is permanent. `rotate` returns a replacement `runner_token` once; save it and update the host. `self_test` queues a sandbox check; the runner receives it on its next heartbeat and reports later. The response confirms the request, not the result. Revoked runners return 409 `UZ-RUN-018`.

Policy changes reach the runner on its next heartbeat. Repeating the current policy has no effect; revoked runners return 400. Labels replace the entire set, using enrollment limits. Duplicates are removed in their original order; an empty list clears labels. Revoked runners' labels remain editable. The response includes labels when supplied.

get.description:
Lists a runner's work assignments newest first, with fleet outcomes and failure reasons. Requires platform administrator access. Continue with `next_cursor` as `starting_after`.

`destination` is `available` for a fleet in your account, `fleet_deleted` after deletion, or `not_permitted` in another account. Fleet and event fields become null when their records are removed.

Completed assignments remain for 30 days after settlement. Running or renewing assignments are retained. Assignments abandoned by a dead runner expire after the same window, then receive their own retention window.

Acquisition and release activity remains for 30 days after each event; other runner lifecycle activity is retained. Lifetime counters remain unchanged when history is removed.

get.description:
Streams fleet activity using Server-Sent Events (SSE). Each message has `id`, `event`, and JSON `data`; `event` matches `data.kind`.

The first message is `hello`, with `fleet_ids` containing this fleet and empty `counters`. It confirms subscription readiness. No `hello` means the live subscription is unavailable.

Activity includes:
- `event_admitted`: accepted chat message, with `event_id`, `actor`, `event_type`, `message`, and `created_at`.
- `event_received`: run started, with the same fields; `message` appears for user messages.
- `event_complete`: the saved event without fleet or workspace identifiers, plus `fleet_status` and `pending_approvals`. `final_reply` appears up to 64 KiB; otherwise fetch event details.
- `gate_opened` and `gate_resolved`: `gate_id`, `event_id`, and `pending_approvals`. Requests outside a run use null `event_id`. Resolutions add `status` and `resolved_by`.
- `chunk`, `tool_call_started`, `tool_call_progress`, `tool_call_completed`, and `context_progress`: live reply and tool activity. Tool messages include `event_id` and `name`. Newer runners add a unique `call_id` per call, shared across its messages.
- Completed tools from newer runners add `status` (`succeeded`, `failed`, or `interrupted`), the first and last five output lines, and `output_line_count`. These lines are `output_head` and `output_tail`; process calls also include `exit_code`.

`catching_up` reports missed messages through `dropped`; zero means the count is unknown. Reload saved events after this signal. Identifiers restart at zero per connection; `Last-Event-ID` is ignored. `hello` and `catching_up` use zero without advancing activity identifiers. Heartbeats arrive after 15 idle seconds, with `kind: heartbeat` and no identifier.

Access is checked every 15 seconds. `access_revoked` sends `data: {"kind":"access_revoked","error_code":"UZ-AUTH-001"}` and closes; do not reconnect. Failed access checks close the stream after about one minute; recover as after a disconnect. At capacity, 503 `UZ-API-002` includes `Retry-After`. Fetch missed events before reconnecting.

total.description: How many turns the thread holds in total. Never populated.

call_id.description:
Which call of the run this frame belongs to, 1 to 64 bytes: every frame
of one call carries the same value.

exit_code.description: The process's exit code, for a call that ran one.

ms.description: How long it took, in milliseconds.

output_head.description: The output's first lines, at most 5 lines and 1024 bytes.

output_line_count.description: How many lines the whole output had.

output_tail.description: The output's last lines, at most 5 lines and 1024 bytes.

arguments.description: Every argument the call was made with, secret values masked. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

call_id.description: Tool call identifier from the conversation, in `{fence}:{n}` format. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

output.description: Everything the call returned. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

output_line_count.description: How many lines the whole output had, before any cut. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

truncated.description: Whether the output was cut to fit 65536 bytes. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

truncated_arguments.description: Whether the arguments were cut to fit 65536 bytes. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

ToolCallProgress.description: A long-running tool is still working, so a reader's spinner survives it.

call_id.description:
Which call of the run this frame belongs to, 1 to 64 bytes: every frame
of one call carries the same value.

elapsed_ms.description: How long it has been running, in milliseconds.

ToolCallRecord.description: One finished call as the runner records it.

arguments.description:
Every argument the call was made with, secret values masked. At most
65536 bytes encoded, with no NUL character.

call_number.description:
Call number within its run, starting at 1. This is `n` in the `{fence}:{n}` identifier
used by activity and saved records.

output.description:
Everything the call returned, at most 65536 bytes, with no NUL
character.

output_line_count.description: How many lines the whole output had, before any cut.

truncated.description: Whether the runner cut the output to fit.

truncated_arguments.description: Whether the runner cut the arguments to fit.

calls.description: The finished calls to keep. A call posted again replaces its record.

fencing_token.description: The lease's fencing token; a holder the fleet has superseded is refused.

skipped_count.description: Records refused for their shape, a bound, or the event's budget. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

stored_count.description: Records written or replaced. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

ToolCallStarted.description:
A tool call started. `args_redacted` contains JSON text with secret values masked, never
the resolved secrets.

call_id.description:
Which call of the run this frame belongs to, 1 to 64 bytes: every frame
of one call carries the same value.

ToolCallStatus.description:
How one tool call ended.

Every call ends exactly once. A call the run never finished, after a crash,
a kill or a timeout, ends `interrupted`. So no call is left running in a
browser or missing from the record.

ToolTrace.description: Every call one run made, oldest first.

omitted_call_count.description: Calls the run made past the 200 listed.

ToolTraceCall.description: One call in a run's trace.

arguments.description:
The arguments the call was made with, secret values masked. At most
2048 bytes encoded, no string or key inside longer than 256 bytes, and
no NUL character anywhere.

call_id.description:
Call number starting at 1, as a decimal string. Other formats are dropped. The server
adds `{fence}:` to match the activity stream's identifier.

duration_ms.description: How long the call took, in milliseconds.

exit_code.description: The process's exit code, for a call that ran one.

output_head.description:
The output's first lines, at most 5 lines and 1024 bytes. Absent when
the call returned nothing or the trace ran out of room for it.

output_line_count.description: How many lines the whole output had.

output_tail.description:
The output's last lines, at most 5 lines and 1024 bytes. Absent when
the head already holds the whole output.

Turn.description:
One earlier exchange in the fleet's thread: what was asked, and what the
fleet answered.

answer.description: The fleet's answer, or the fixed text a reply-less or failed run reads as.

message.description: The event's message, as `event::message_of` reads it.

UpdateModelEntryRequest.description: `PATCH /v1/tenants/me/models/{id}` — point an entry at another model.

Usage.description: Creator-visible usage; unknown provider figures remain absent.

knowledge.description: Context knowledge measured by the server, independent of runner estimates.

provider_cost_nanos.description: Physical provider cost, absent while unknown.

verification_code.description: The six digits a person read out of the browser.

VerifySessionResponse.description: What a redeemed login hands back.

nonce.description: The nonce used to encrypt this credential.

View.description: One schedule, as the tenant surface renders it.

description.description:
The expression in words, with the zone it is read in, for example
`At 9:00 AM (Asia/Kolkata)`.

etag.description: Current `ETag` covering the selected recipe, setup, and instance overrides.

last_error.description: Why the last push failed, when one did.

message.description: What the fleet is asked to do.

next_run_at.description:
When it next runs, computed by the server from the expression and its
zone. Null unless `run_state` is `scheduled`.

once.description: Whether it retires after its first fire. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

oneOf.description: Explicit instance overlay, omitted when the pinned recipe is inherited.

run_state.description: Whether the schedule will run, as the server reads it now.

source.description:
Who made it: `api` for a person, `trigger` for the fleet's own
document, `fleet` for the fleet while it ran. Only a `fleet` schedule
can be changed by the fleet. Beta: this field may change shape before it is stable.

status.description: What the operator wants it to be doing.

sync.description:
How far agentsfleet has brought the external scheduler in line.

A schedule can save without registering. This field shows you that
state.

timezone.description: The zone that expression is read in.

Visibility.description:
Who reads a stored entry: its own fleet, or every fleet in the workspace
granted to read shared memory.

WaitingInvite.description: One invite waiting for the caller's address.

id.description: The invite's identifier, which the accept route names.

WebhookUrl.description: Public manual-webhook address for one declared source.

WorkspaceAccount.description: The account a listed workspace belongs to.

owner_name.description:
What a person calls the account: its owner's display name, or the
account's own name when the owner has none.

WorkspaceMember.description:
One member of a workspace's account, as its thread names senders.

No address: every member of an account can read this list, and a name is
all a thread needs.

actor.description:
The actor their messages record, `steer:<subject>`: what a thread
row's `actor` equals when this member sent it.

display_name.description: Their name, `null` when the identity provider supplied none.

WorkspaceModel.description: A priced explicit selection owned by the workspace's billing account.

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum output tokens; omitted when model settings are not configured.

ref.description:
Model selection reference, including an explicit shared platform default. Use it
unchanged.

WorkspaceSummary.description: One workspace as the list shows it.

account.description: The account it belongs to, which is how a dashboard groups the list.

created_at.description: When it was created; the walk's sort key.

name.description:
Its name — `null` on rows older than naming, emitted either way for
the tenant module's null rule.

role.description: The caller's role in that account: `owner` or `member`.

WorkspacesResponse.description:
`GET /v1/tenants/me/workspaces` — one page of the workspaces across every
account the caller holds.

items.description: The rows on this page, oldest first.

next_cursor.description: Where the next page resumes, or `null` on the last page.

tenant_id.description:
The caller's own account — the authoritative resolution, carried so a
client can pin its local state to the right person. Items from accounts
the caller joined name theirs in `account`.

total.description:
Always `null`: the walk never counts, and the key stays because a
client may already branch on its presence.

BearerAuth.description: Send a dashboard session token, an account API key (`agt_t`), or a command-line credential (`afc_`) as a Bearer token. Each endpoint lists accepted credential types.

RunnerBearerAuth.description: Runner token beginning with agt_r, returned once by POST /v1/runners
